title: The Choir of the Glass Steppe
premise: When the crown of Veyra declares a purge of all magic-bearers, Silas Whitlock — a mercenary whose god fell silent twenty years ago, leaving him with fading charms and a hollow oath — is betrayed by a client and branded a heretic. Fleeing the hunt, he discovers that the queen's new inquisitor is buying souls wholesale and selling them to a court beneath the mountain that keeps the realm's seasons turning. Among the stolen souls is Wren, a young singer whose gift once saved Silas's life and whom he swore to protect. To free her, Silas must descend into the Glass Steppe's buried court, confront the truth that his silent god was devoured to fuel that court, and choose between restoring his own divinity or spending it to buy Wren back. He spends it — dying mortal but free, while Wren carries their shared song into a world where magic must finally be lived openly rather than outlawed.
about_author: T. M. Reyes is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write from a farmhouse on the moors, accompanied by an opinionated cat and a growing collection of broken bells.

chapters.title: Small Charms for Hard Winters
chapters.summary: Silas Whitlock sells a luck-knot to a dockworker in the smuggler's quarter, hiding how weak his magic has grown since his god went silent. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: weary tenderness — he still serves people, even without divine backing.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Heralds read the Purge Edict: all gifted persons must surrender for 'soul assessment.' Silas watches a neighbor dragged away and burns his ledgers. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: cold dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Wren's Voice
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: fifteen years earlier, a child named Wren sang a dying Silas back to life with borrowed song-magic, binding them together. POV: Silas (memory). Emotional beat: grief-tinged warmth; establishes the debt that drives him.

chapters.title: The Client Who Sold Him
chapters.summary: A wealthy patron hires Silas for one last charm, then betrays him to inquisitors to buy her family's safety. Silas escapes through the sewers, wounded. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: bitter betrayal; the hunt becomes personal.

chapters.title: Inquisitor Vael
chapters.summary: Introducing Crown Inquisitor Vael, who harvests souls with courteous efficiency and genuinely believes she is saving the realm. POV: Vael. Emotional beat: chilling conviction — the antagonist who thinks she's the hero.

chapters.title: The Hollow Choir
chapters.summary: Silas finds refuge with the Hollow Choir, an underground network of hidden magicians led by Mother Ash. There he learns souls are being sent beneath the mountain. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: cautious hope among fellow outcasts.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Eats
chapters.summary: Mother Ash reveals the bargain: the subterranean Glass Court powers the seasons, paid in souls since the old gods were consumed. Silas realizes his god was among them. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: shattering revelation reframing his silence as theft.

chapters.title: Wren Is Taken
chapters.summary: Vael's raid captures Wren during a Choir concert used as cover. Silas arrives too late, holding only her dropped ribbon. POV: alternating Silas/Wren. Emotional beat: devastating failure; duty and love collide.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage
chapters.summary: To reach the mountain's depths, Silas bargains with a ferryman of the dead: his remaining charms, his name, and a memory of his god's face. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grim sacrifice; identity begins eroding.

chapters.title: Descent Through Bone
chapters.summary: Silas descends the ossuary stair beneath the Steppe, passing murals depicting the devouring of the gods. He fights off soul-hungry wraiths using almost nothing. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: isolation and dwindling selfhood.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Silas reaches the Glass Court: a cathedral of frozen singers who power the seasons by eternally performing. He spots Wren being fitted into the choir. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Regent of Glass
chapters.summary: The Court's Regent offers Silas restoration of his godhood if he joins willingly and brings more souls above. It shows him what he could be again. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: seductive temptation at his weakest moment.

chapters.title: Wren, Singing
chapters.summary: Wren's POV inside the choir: she retains herself by singing variations the Court cannot fully absorb, quietly unbinding other captives note by note. Emotional beat: defiant resilience; she is no damsel.

chapters.title: Vael Descends
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Vael arrives to negotiate a fresh soul-contract, revealing the crown's founders made the original bargain. She and Silas, both trapped in others' sins, circle each other. POV: Vael. Emotional beat: reluctant recognition between enemies.

chapters.title: The First Crack
chapters.summary: Wren's off-key rebellion cracks one pane of the Court; a captive soul escapes upward, and winter falters over the Steppe. Panic spreads above and below. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: dangerous hope — freedom has costs.

chapters.title: Bargain and Betrayal
chapters.summary: Silas pretends to accept the Regent's offer to get close to Wren, but Vael exposes the ruse to save her own contract. Silas is bound into the choir beside Wren. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: despair at the lowest point.

chapters.title: Duet in Chains
chapters.summary: Bound together, Silas and Wren harmonize deliberately, weaving his old oath into the song. The Court cannot digest a freely given promise. Panes begin failing across the cathedral. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: love against duty, literally sung.

chapters.title: The God Remembered
chapters.summary: Inside the collapsing choir, Silas recovers the memory he sold: his god's face — which is his own. His divinity was never lost, only buried here. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed at terrible cost.

chapters.title: Breaking the Glass
chapters.summary: Climax: Silas shatters his own divinity to free every soul at once, including his god's remnant. The Court collapses; Vael chooses, at last, to hold the exit open rather than seal it. POV: all three. Emotional beat: sacrificial triumph.

chapters.title: Seasons Unbound
chapters.summary: The survivors surface to a world where seasons now drift without masters — frightening, alive, ungoverned. Vael publicly confesses the crown's bargain and is arrested by her own soldiers. POV: Vael. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, imperfectly won.

chapters.title: Mortal Hands
chapters.summary: Silas, now wholly mortal, tends the freed and frightened magicians alongside Wren. He can no longer work charms, only ordinary kindness. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: quiet grief transmuted into peace.

chapters.title: The Choir of the Open Air
chapters.summary: On the Steppe at first thaw, Wren leads a choir of the freed in open daylight, magic sung without shame. Silas listens, unnamed and unimportant and content. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: resolution — identity, love, and justice reconciled under an unowned sky.
